newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni tribesmen let German hostages phone home.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni tribesmen let German hostages phone home.

text.p: Yemeni tribesmen holding seven Germans hostage have allowed them to telephone their families as Yemeni forces tightened a siege of the area where they are thought to be held, a security official said on Sunday.
The source said the kidnappers "allowed the hostages to telephone their families in Germany on cellular telephones".
The men were kidnapped on Monday while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces.

"As negotiations continue with the kidnappers by mediators representing the government, security forces have since last night tightened the siege on the area where the captives are believed held," he told Reuters.
The source said the negotiations "centre on how to release the hostages without the government making any concessions to the kidnappers".
On Thursday, one of the hostages, a German tour guide, told a Hamburg radio station they were being treated "fairly well".

Official sources said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.
They said the abductors had telephoned local authorities to demand 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom for their release.
But police in Hadramaut, 770 km (480 miles) east of Sanaa, denied the kidnappers were demanding a ransom.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
